summary: GRAVEYARD underwriting pass worked all 12 b03 companies in parallel. Six have sufficiently current primary financial evidence for Chief treatment in this pass; six remain exact issuer-primary acquisition tasks rather than vague research. No score/rank proposal is made.

materialFindings.finding: 2025 geographic revenue concentration is material: Taiwan $1.155bn, China $451m and Korea $446m. Semiconductor-test exposure is therefore structurally tied to Asian semiconductor production and customer geography.

FY2025 revenue grew 15% to $1.894bn; operating cash flow was $602m; cash ended at $1.8bn before expected $612m Mentee acquisition outlay. New high-volume Surround ADAS US OEM win and Volkswagen robotaxi roadmap are disclosed catalysts.

Historical primary filing establishes extreme platform concentration: Uber was 71% of 2023 revenue. A 2025 financing release showed $86m December 2024 financing and runway then estimated through end-2026. Current concentration/runway must be refreshed before reproducible treatment.

At June 30 2026 cash+short-term investments were $1.217bn; six-month revenue only $3m versus $493m net loss. Shares outstanding increased to 1.998bn from 1.943bn at year-end 2025. Survival runway is substantial but commercialization and dilution risk remain material.

FY2025 revenue $1.104bn, net income $181m and backlog $1.4bn. Q1 FY2026 backlog reached $1.6bn, cash/short investments $501m, and management disclosed first data-center megaproject order plus large LNG award.

FY2025 revenue $31.5m against $664m net loss and $459.6m operating cash use; financing supplied $1.300bn net common-stock issuance proceeds. Commercial optionality is paired with exceptionally high dilution/financing dependence.

Current primary quarterly evidence shows Electrical Americas order momentum/backlog strength and Aerospace backlog growth; company explicitly serves data center, utility, industrial, aerospace and mobility electrification markets.
